editorial.headline: Animal Health’s Specialist Support Services
editorial.standfirst: A defined home for the banks, transport, optical work and specialist support that sit behind animal health services.
editorial.body:
KBLI 75009 covers the supporting infrastructure that allows animal health services to function beyond a conventional clinical encounter: animal blood-transfusion units and blood banks; eye banks; companion-animal sperm banks; organ-transplant, cell and tissue banks; animal optical services; animal ambulances; and other supporting animal-health services. Its centre of gravity is not a single treatment, but the systems, storage, movement and specialist support that make animal care possible. The wording also leaves room for other supporting animal-health services, while its examples consistently point to specialised support functions.

Registration is open at every listed scale—Micro, Small, Medium and Large—so the record does not confine this activity to one size of operator. That breadth does not widen the activity’s subject matter: the enterprise must still be built around the defined animal-health support functions. Nationally, it is marked TERBUKA, or open to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. On this record, foreign capital can therefore hold the entire permitted ownership interest; the stated basis is Presidential Regulations 10/2021 and 49/2021.

In Bali, a PT PMA can register this activity because its medium-high classification sits outside the permanent moratorium for low and medium-low risk activities. That is the decisive local point: the provincial rule is island-wide and permanent, but it blocks PMA registration only in the lower-risk categories named in that rule. The Bali record expressly says this activity survives the moratorium and is registrable by a PT PMA. Its local position is therefore the recorded consequence of its classification under the risk rule.

The national and Bali conclusions need to be read together. Nationally, foreign ownership may reach 100%, and Bali does not reverse that result for this activity: it remains registrable there by a PT PMA. The relevant Bali explanation is the activity’s placement outside the moratorium’s low and medium-low risk boundary. For founders, the practical reading is clear: an animal-health support business within this defined scope can be structured with foreign investment nationally and registered in Bali under the stated classification.
